# eslint-plugin-use-everywhere

> Four ESLint rules for the `use-everywhere` mistakes that are silent at runtime:
> a bus factory called inside a component, a dynamic bus name, a value in shared
> state that structured clone cannot carry, and a leader effect capturing render
> state. Each produces code that looks correct and syncs nothing, which is why
> the types cannot catch them and a linter has to. Flat config only.

## Install

    npm install -D eslint-plugin-use-everywhere

Peer: `eslint >= 9`. This package is configured, not imported into app code.

## Use

Flat config, in `eslint.config.js`:

```js
import useEverywhere from 'eslint-plugin-use-everywhere';

export default [useEverywhere.configs.recommended];
```

The recommended config carries no `files` key, so it applies wherever you place
it — put it after a `files` block of your own if the project mixes languages.

To pick rules individually instead:

```js
import useEverywhere from 'eslint-plugin-use-everywhere';

export default [
  {
    plugins: { 'use-everywhere': useEverywhere },
    rules: {
      'use-everywhere/define-at-module-scope': 'error',
      'use-everywhere/no-dynamic-name': 'error',
      'use-everywhere/structured-clone-safe': 'error',
      'use-everywhere/leader-effect-captures': 'warn',
    },
  },
];
```

## Rules

| Rule | Recommended | What it catches |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `define-at-module-scope` | error | `defineStore`, `defineChannel` or `createNamespace` called anywhere but the top level of a module. Inside a component it builds a new bus every render, and the page syncs nothing while looking fine. |
| `no-dynamic-name` | error | A bus name that is not a string literal, a module-scope `const` string, or an imported binding. A computed name means two tabs can silently disagree about which bus they are on. |
| `structured-clone-safe` | error | Values in shared state that the structured clone algorithm cannot carry — functions, class instances, DOM nodes, symbols. The write throws in the tab that made it and nowhere else. |
| `leader-effect-captures` | warn | Values declared in a component that a `useLeaderEffect` callback reads. A warning rather than an error: a captured value that never changes is harmless, and the rule cannot tell the difference, so it argues rather than blocks. |
